questions.stem: Local government in Nigeria is described as the third tier of government because it

options.text: controls the armed forces and the Central Bank
is the level of administration closest to the people, below the federal and state governments
is appointed directly by the United Nations
has power to amend the 1999 Constitution on its own

questions.explanation: Nigeria's federation has three constitutionally recognised levels: federal, state and local. Section 7 guarantees a system of local government by democratically elected councils. It is 'third' because it sits below the other two and handles grassroots functions listed in the Fourth Schedule.

distractorRationale.a: Defence and the Central Bank are exclusive federal matters
distractorRationale.c: Local councils are Nigerian constitutional bodies, not UN agencies
distractorRationale.d: Constitutional amendment is a function of the National Assembly and State Houses of Assembly under section 9

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, section 7

questions.stem: The most important source of revenue for Nigerian local governments is

options.text: profits from overseas investments
statutory allocation from the Federation Account
tolls collected on federal highways
export duties on crude oil shipped by the council

questions.explanation: A share of the Federation Account, paid through the State Joint Local Government Account (section 162), dwarfs rates, licences and market fees. That dominance is why delayed or diverted statutory allocation can stop a council from paying staff. Rates and licences matter, but they are not the largest source.

distractorRationale.a: Local councils do not run overseas investment portfolios as a principal revenue source
distractorRationale.c: Federal highway tolls, where they exist, accrue to the federal government
distractorRationale.d: Oil export is a federal matter; councils do not ship crude

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, section 162

questions.stem: A major feature of the 1976 local government reform in Nigeria was the

options.text: abolition of all local councils in favour of native authorities only
introduction of a uniform, elected, multi-purpose local government system nationwide
transfer of the armed forces to local government control
creation of 36 states to replace local councils

questions.explanation: The 1976 Guidelines replaced a patchwork of native authorities and appointed sole administrators with a single-tier, uniform system of elected councils, a standard list of functions, federal statutory allocation, and 301 local government areas. The present 774 councils grew from that structure.

distractorRationale.a: The reform moved away from native-authority administration, not towards it
distractorRationale.d: States are the second tier; 36 states were not a 1976 local-government measure

questions.stem: State interference in local government in Nigeria is commonly shown by

options.text: the conduct of federal elections by INEC
the dissolution of elected councils and the operation of the State Joint Local Government Account
the sitting of the Supreme Court in Abuja
the existence of 109 senators

questions.explanation: Governors have frequently dissolved elected councils and installed caretaker committees, contrary to the spirit of section 7. Through the joint account in section 162(6), states also control the timing and amount of statutory funds that actually reach the councils. Those two practices are the textbook illustrations of state interference.

distractorRationale.a: INEC's conduct of federal elections is not state interference in local government
distractorRationale.c: The location of the Supreme Court is unrelated to council autonomy
distractorRationale.d: The number of senators is a federal legislative fact, not a local-government problem

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, sections 7 and 162

questions.stem: The functions of local government in Nigeria are listed in

options.text: Chapter IV of the 1999 Constitution
the Fourth Schedule to the 1999 Constitution
the Exclusive Legislative List only
the Treaty of Lagos 1975

questions.explanation: The Fourth Schedule sets out the main functions of a local government council — markets, local roads, refuse, rates, licensing, registration of births and deaths, and participation in primary education and primary health. Chapter IV is fundamental rights; the Exclusive List is federal; the Treaty of Lagos created ECOWAS.

distractorRationale.a: Chapter IV contains fundamental human rights, not council functions
distractorRationale.c: The Exclusive Legislative List assigns powers to the National Assembly
distractorRationale.d: The Treaty of Lagos established ECOWAS, an international organisation

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, Fourth Schedule

questions.stem: Nigeria currently has 774 local government areas, including the area councils of the Federal Capital Territory.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: True. The 1999 Constitution lists 768 local government areas in the 36 states plus six area councils in the FCT, giving 774. The 1976 reform began with 301; later creations produced the present total. Examiners treat 774 as a required figure.

distractorRationale.b: The figure 774 is the standard constitutional total; 301 was the 1976 starting number, not the current one

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, First Schedule
